title: Asymmetric Burst Control Slate for Dedicated GPU Pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design ticket for a compact, asymmetric burst control UI for Redwood Dedicated GPU pools. The goal is to give operators fine-grained short-term burst allocations and asymmetric downscaling knobs that prioritize maintaining latency SLOs for critical routes while reclaiming capacity for cheaper backfill workloads. This design should dovetail with existing pool health timelines and autoscaling sliders but introduce a separate burst budget timeline, granular per-route burst caps, and a rapid rollback control for safety. Considerations: visual density for fleet operators, discoverability for on-call engineers, how burst interacts with reserved capacity and canary rollouts, accessibility, and localization.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype screens for pool-level burst panel and per-route burst table are reviewed and approved by PM and Eng
Interactions documented: create/edit burst window, asymmetric scale-down curve, per-route priority assignment, emergency-revoke action
High-fidelity Figma prototype links included and annotated with measurements and tokenized copy
Hand-off ready spec (components, states, accessibility notes) uploaded to Drive and linked from ticket
UX copy reviewed and microcopy updated in console localization file
decisions: Separate burst budget from autoscale to avoid coupling autoscaler heuristics with manual operator overrides
Expose asymmetric ramp-down curve (fast reclaim for low-priority routes, slow for critical routes) rather than a single decay parameter
Emergency revoke action will trigger a documented safe-eviction flow and an audit event in logs
